This bug is still present, and nothing in the Melogold code has fixed it. Paths below are relative to /Users/maxim/Documents/melogold/melogoldAndroid. Note: the /Users/maxim/Documents/vitunefork/melogoldAndroid path in the task does not exist, so I read the melogold copy.

1. Downloads live in the OS-purgeable cacheDir.
   - app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/service/PlayerService.kt:1335 sets DEFAULT_CACHE_DIRECTORY = "exoplayer".
   - PlayerService.kt:1339-1354 createCache() puts the SimpleCache at `cacheDir.resolve(directoryName)` (:1349).
   - Android's low-storage cleanup, "Clear cache" and OEM cleaners (MIUI, Samsung Device Care) can delete everything there. This matches #1057 (9 GB lost, "I did not clear the app's storage") and #1476 (2026-09-05, "offline list deletes itself at random times").

2. Downloads share the LRU budget with normal playback.
   - PlayerService.kt:1344-1347 uses LeastRecentlyUsedCacheEvictor(size.bytes) unless the setting is Unlimited.
   - app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/preferences/DataPreferences.kt:16 sets the default to 2GB.
   - core/data/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/core/data/enums/ExoPlayerDiskCacheSize.kt:6-17 lists sizes from 32MB to 8GB.
   - Result: normal listening pushes explicit downloads out.

3. PrecacheService writes into that same cache.
   - app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/service/PrecacheService.kt:150-158 gets `binder?.cache` from PlayerService.
   - PrecacheService.kt:170-180 builds DownloadManager(cache = that same cache).
   - Nothing pins or protects the downloaded bytes.

4. There is no durable "downloaded" state.
   - The Offline playlist is computed from whatever is fully cached at the moment. See app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/ui/screens/builtinplaylist/BuiltInPlaylistSongs.kt:82-90, which filters songsWithContentLength by `binder?.isCached(it) ?: false`.
   - PlayerService.kt:1239-1240 checks cache.isCached(id, 0, contentLength).
   - app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/utils/CacheState.kt:83-104 does the same check.
   - Any evicted span, a null binder, or a changed contentLength removes the song from Offline.
   - The contentLength comes from a Format row that is rewritten on every resolve (PlayerService.kt:1437-1451).

5. The download index and the cache drift apart.
   - When the cache is wiped, Media3's DownloadIndex, stored in the separate databases/ dir via StandaloneDatabaseProvider (PlayerService.kt:1338), still says COMPLETED.
   - Hiding or deleting a song calls only `cache.removeResource` (app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/ui/screens/home/HomeSongs.kt:275, :336) and never sendRemoveDownload.

6. The cache belongs to PlayerService.
   - PlayerService.kt:299 creates it, and PlayerService.kt:438 calls cache.release() in onDestroy.
   - PrecacheService keeps the resolved instance forever (PrecacheService.kt:281, lazy runBlocking).
   - So closing or killing the player while downloads are queued leaves the DownloadManager writing into a released cache. Downloads then fail or end up half-written, which adds to the "downloads vanish" reports.

7. The UI has no separate downloads storage. app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/ui/screens/settings/CacheSettings.kt:83-125 has one "song cache" group with a max size and a pause switch. The download menu entry is a "pre_cache" entry in app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/ui/components/themed/MediaItemMenu.kt:749-760.

8. Desktop clients (melogoldLinux, melogoldWindows, melogoldiOSmacOS) are still stubs with only a README and assets, so no desktop code has this bug yet.

This matters for Melogold's core use case. Censored Russian tracks may also get taken down on YouTube, so a download that can't be evicted is often the only lasting copy. That applies to Music-catalogue tracks and to plain-YouTube re-uploads alike, because both are keyed by videoId.
verify:offline-eviction.fix_idea:
1. Split storage into two caches.
   - Keep the streaming cache as it is: cacheDir/exoplayer with the LRU evictor.
   - Add a download store: a second SimpleCache at filesDir/downloads with NoOpCacheEvictor.
   - Offer getExternalFilesDirs() as an optional storage location so SD cards can be used.
   - Both caches can share one StandaloneDatabaseProvider, because SimpleCache tables are keyed by uid.
   - Create both as process-wide singletons in MainApplication/Dependencies, not in PlayerService. Then PlayerService.onDestroy (:438) no longer releases the cache under PrecacheService, and PrecacheService no longer needs to bind to PlayerService, so remove BlockingDeferredCache (PrecacheService.kt:91-158, 276-322).

2. Point downloads at the new store. PrecacheService's DownloadManager (PrecacheService.kt:170-180) uses downloadCache as both its cache and its CacheDataSource target.

3. Change the playback read chain.
   - In ConditionalCacheDataSourceFactory (CacheState.kt:107), when downloadCache holds the key fully, return a read-only CacheDataSource over downloadCache: setCacheWriteDataSinkFactory(null) with an upstream that throws, so playback works offline.
   - Otherwise use the existing streaming chain.
   - The resolver fast path at PlayerService.kt:1384-1396 must check downloadCache first and skip yt-dlp and the Format rewrite for downloaded songs.

4. Store an explicit download state.
   - Use DownloadManager.downloadIndex (STATE_COMPLETED), or add a Room table Download(songId, itag, contentLength, bytes, downloadedAt).
   - Build the Offline playlist, isCached(), PlaylistDownloadIcon and the menu from that state instead of the cache.isCached(0, contentLength) probe (BuiltInPlaylistSongs.kt:82-90, PlayerService.kt:1239, CacheState.kt:83-104).
   - At startup, check each completed download against the cache. If bytes are missing, mark it "needs re-download" and offer "Re-download missing" instead of silently dropping it.

5. Remove downloads properly. Deleting or hiding a song (HomeSongs.kt:275, :336) and a new "Remove download" menu entry must call DownloadService.sendRemoveDownload so the index and store stay in sync.

6. Update Settings > Cache (CacheSettings.kt). Add a separate "Downloads" group with space used, location, and "Delete all downloads". Relabel the existing LRU setting as "Streaming cache" and state that it never affects downloads.

7. Migrate existing data once. For keys that the old DownloadIndex marks COMPLETED and that are fully present in cacheDir/exoplayer, copy them into the new store with CacheWriter, reading from the old cache so no network is needed. Then drop them from the old cache.

8. Optional, and part of a separate cluster: "Export as file" through SAF (MediaStore Music/Melogold) so users keep real .opus/.m4a copies outside the app.

9. Desktop clients: when they are built, put downloads in the app-data directory (~/Library/Application Support/Melogold, %APPDATA%\Melogold, $XDG_DATA_HOME/melogold), never in Caches, Temp or XDG_CACHE_HOME.

Effort: M for items 1-7. It grows toward L if the user-chosen SAF folder and file export are included.

Auto shows the bottom bar when the window is under 600dp wide (LocalConfiguration.screenWidthDp or material3-adaptive), and the rail on tablets, landscape and ChromeOS. 7. Customisable tabs. Move the long-press dialog to Settings > Appearance > Navigation. Show an ordered list with ReorderHandle drag-reorder and on/off toggles. Store the order under a new key such as "home/order" in the existing visibleTabs JSON map, so current hidden-tab data keeps working without a migration. Allow at most 5 tabs in the bar; the rest go into a Library tab (chips) or a "More" sheet. Keep long-press as a shortcut.

   - Home (Quick Picks and Discover merged)
   - Search, promoted to a tab, with a first-class "YouTube videos" results filter. This serves the uncensored-source goal (re-uploads, covers, live recordings).
   - Library (Songs, Playlists, Artists, Albums, Local, and "Imported" for Apple Music / Spotify / Yandex imports)
   - Account (sync, QR linking of devices, Settings)

9. Right-side option. When railSide == End, put the rail second in the Row. Doing only this part is effort S.

Effort: M (2-3 days) for a minimum version: a bottom bar on Home only, the inset and mini-player fix, and the preference toggle. L (1-2 weeks) for everything: adaptive layout, top bars on detail screens, swipe pager, hide on scroll, the reorderable tab settings screen and the new information architecture.

1) Restore overwrites the live database in place with no checks. See app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/ui/screens/settings/DatabaseSettings.kt:59-81. It runs `Database.checkpoint()` and `Database.internal.close()`, then `FileOutputStream(Database.internal.path)`, which truncates the file before copying the chosen file over data.db. Then it calls `stopService` and `exitProcess(0)` on Room's multi-threaded queryExecutor (Database.kt:1136). Nothing checks the SQLite header, `user_version`, the Room identityHash or integrity. There is also no temp file, atomic rename or rollback.
 - When other code touches the database during the copy, this probably causes the corruption users see. Candidates are the Flows on this same screen (:39-43), PlayerService, and the MediaStore worker, which writes every 5 s (ui/screens/home/HomeLocalSongs.kt:124-158). Room either reopens the database or keeps a connection whose -wal/-shm files belong to the old database. The upstream #268 log shows exactly this: SQLiteDatabaseCorruptException "database disk image is malformed" on thread arch_disk_io.
 - If the file is not SQLite, for example the .zip that users attach in #268, data.db becomes garbage. On the next open, SupportSQLiteOpenHelper.Callback.onCorruption deletes the database, and the library is wiped silently.
 - If the backup's schema is newer, or its identity hash differs (a ViMusic→ViTune database, #1283, or a RiMusic database), Room throws on every launch. The app is stuck in a crash loop and the only way out is clearing app data (#1300, #1283).
 - If `openInputStream` returns null, the database is still closed and the process exits with no message. This matches "silently does nothing" (#554).
 - `DatabaseDependency.reload()` (Database.kt:97-101) cannot fix any of this in-process. The companion delegate at Database.kt:105-107 is fixed at startup, so reload() never switches to the new database.

 - The backup contains everything. That includes the PipedSession token in plain text (models/PipedSession.kt; the token was leaked publicly in the #268 comments), QueuedMediaItem Parcel blobs, which depend on the device, and the `local:` songs.
 - The file name is still "ViTune_backup_" (:151).

AndroidManifest.xml:48 sets `allowBackup="true"` with no dataExtractionRules or fullBackupContent, so Google Auto Backup takes whatever is in filesDir. I have not verified it, but the Python/yt-dlp files may push this over the 25 MB quota, and Auto Backup would then be skipped.

It never deletes rows that are gone from MediaStore. After a restore, the old phone's local songs stay, and when IDs collide on the new phone the metadata is stale. The Local tab reads the database, not MediaStore (:83-89).

A) Safe restore (M):
 (1) Copy the SAF stream into cacheDir/restore/candidate. If this fails, show a toast; the live database is untouched.
 (2) Check the first bytes. "SQLite format 3\0" means an old ViTune/ViMusic .db. "PK\3\4" means a Melogold backup zip.
 (3) Open the candidate read-only with SQLiteDatabase.openDatabase(OPEN_READONLY) and an error handler that does not delete the file. Run `PRAGMA quick_check`. Reject `user_version` > 30 with the message "made by a newer Melogold, update first". Require the Song, Playlist and SongPlaylistMap tables.
 (4) Do a trial migration on a throwaway Room instance of DatabaseInitializer named "restore_candidate.db", with the same addMigrations list, and force `openHelper.writableDatabase`. Migration or identity-hash errors (#1283) become a clean error message instead of a crash loop.
 (5) Clean the candidate: DELETE FROM PipedSession and QueuedMediaItem, and delete `local:%` songs that are missing from the current MediaStore.
 (6) Swap the file at the next cold start instead of in place. Write filesDir/pending_restore.db plus a marker, stop the player the way OtherSettings.kt:329-337 does, and relaunch through a PendingIntent before exiting. In MainApplication.onCreate, before DatabaseDependency is first used: rename data.db to data.db.prev, remove -wal/-shm/-journal, rename the candidate to data.db, and restore data.db.prev if Room fails to open.
 Later, an ATTACH-based "merge instead of overwrite" import would allow restoring without a restart, once the companion delegate at Database.kt:105-107 is fixed.

B) Clean, portable export (S):
 - Take the snapshot inside `DatabaseDependency.instance.runInTransaction{}` (BEGIN IMMEDIATE blocks writers) and copy data.db plus data.db-wal to cache. Open the copy, remove PipedSession, QueuedMediaItem and optionally local songs, then VACUUM. VACUUM INTO is not available because minSdk is 24.
 - Write a zip: manifest.json {format, appVersionCode, dbVersion, identityHash, createdAt}, data.db, and preferences.json (a typed dump of SharedPreferences("preferences").all, skipping device-specific keys). Name it Melogold_backup_*.zip.
 - Better: make the payload the same versioned JSON DTO the Melogold sync server uses. Backups then no longer depend on the Room schema, contain no credentials, and the macOS/Windows/Linux clients can import them. Raw .db import stays as "Import from ViTune/ViMusic".

The code lives at /Users/maxim/Documents/melogold/melogoldAndroid. The path in the task, /Users/maxim/Documents/vitunefork/melogoldAndroid, does not exist. All paths below are relative to the melogoldAndroid folder. git log shows that only the initial import commit (e493388f) has touched the playback, Python, InnerTube and core/data code, so every upstream ViTune bug here is still present.

1. Every yt-dlp failure is reported as an ID mismatch. At service/PlayerService.kt:1408-1413 the code does `runCatching{Dependencies.runDownload}.mapCatching{YouTubeDLResponse.fromString}...getOrNull()` and then `if (info?.id != mediaId) throw VideoIdMismatchException()`. So a bot check ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot"), "Video unavailable", "Requested format is not available", a timeout or DNS failure all show "The returned video ID doesn't match the requested one" (strings.xml:105). The real reason only goes to printStackTrace.

2. The filesize field breaks parsing. utils/YouTubeDLResponse.kt:14-15 declares `@SerialName("filesize") val fileSize: Long` as required, with no default. When yt-dlp returns `filesize: null` (HLS formats, or formats where it only knows `filesize_approx`), decoding fails and the user again sees "ID mismatch".

3. The UI messages are misleading or can never appear.
   - A missing `url` throws UnplayableException (PlayerService.kt:1417). The UI shows that as "The original video source of this song has been deleted" (Thumbnail.kt:256, strings.xml:103).
   - PlayableFormatNotFound, LoginRequired and RestrictedVideo are defined in service/PlaybackExceptions.kt:9-37 but nothing throws them (checked with grep). Their messages never appear.
   - The network message is also dead. Thumbnail.kt:250-252 checks whether `error.cause.cause` is an UnknownHostException. But CatchingDataSourceFactory (utils/ExoPlayer.kt:55-65, applied through `.handleUnknownErrors` at PlayerService.kt:1466) wraps every non-PlaybackException in a generic PlaybackException("Unknown playback error"). That covers HttpDataSourceException(UnknownHost) and the HTTP 403 from googlevideo. So `cause.cause` is never the network exception, and users see "unknown playback error" (#1183, #1258, #1316).

4. Errors are never retried, so any failure stops the song at once. The resolver throws PlaybackException, which is not an IOException. The media3 1.11.1 Loader wraps it in Loader.UnexpectedLoaderException, and DefaultLoadErrorHandlingPolicy treats that as non-retriable. I checked this with javap on media3-exoplayer-1.11.1. As a result, one 403 or one yt-dlp hiccup is fatal.
   - onPlayerError (PlayerService.kt:526-556) only handles HTTP 416.
   - skipOnError defaults to false (preferences/PlayerPreferences.kt:54).
   - `isEligibleForFallback = true` (PlayerService.kt:1077) does nothing for progressive sources.
   - retryIf, withFallback and handleRangeErrors in utils/ExoPlayer.kt:74-181 are never called. They are also buggy: `while (retries < maxRetries)` at :127 counts attempts, not retries, and at :34-36 `filter{range}` keeps only the Range header when it should drop it.

5. Cached stream URLs never expire and survive network changes. Nothing in app/ uses ConnectivityManager or a NetworkCallback, so after a switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, or turning a VPN on or off, the cached URL returns 403. This fits the network-dependent reports (#1244, #534).

6. Playback ignores yt-dlp's per-format `http_headers`. All requests go out with a fixed 2021 user agent, "Firefox/91.0" (utils/ExoPlayer.kt:185-191).

PrecacheService.kt:174-184 sets `chunkLength = null`, so each song is one un-ranged request. yt-dlp itself downloads in 10 MiB chunks (_video.py:3229, :3613). maxParallelDownloads = 3 then produces bursts of extractions (#799: "most songs will not pre-cache").

11. Regular YouTube videos already work when extraction works. The resolver takes any videoId, so re-uploads, covers and recorded (past) live streams play. Streams that are live right now return an HLS manifest. The progressive pipeline cannot play that (the MediaItem URI is youtube.com/watch), and `filesize: null` also turns it into "ID mismatch". - 19e9251bbd re-resolves after a 403 mid-song and fixes RangeHandler.

- 48cf54695a makes the source configurable: InnerTube, yt-dlp, or InnerTube with yt-dlp as fallback.

verify:stream-extraction-failures.fix_idea:
Phase 1: honest errors and self-healing (M, 2-3 days)

(a) In download.py, catch `yt_dlp.utils.DownloadError`/`ExtractorError`/`TransportError` and return `{"error":{"kind","message"}}`. Classify the message into BotCheck, Unavailable/Removed/Private, AgeOrLogin, GeoBlocked, NoFormat, Network or Timeout, and set `socket_timeout`.

(b) In the resolver, map each kind to its own PlaybackException subclass. Throw VideoIdMismatch only when the IDs really differ.

(c) Make `fileSize` nullable and fall back to `filesize_approx`.

(d) In Thumbnail.kt, walk the whole cause chain with findCause and add a "Details / copy diagnostics" row that shows the yt-dlp message. Add a specific message: "YouTube is blocking requests from this network (bot check)".

(e) Stop wrapping IOExceptions in PlaybackException in CatchingDataSourceFactory, so ExoPlayer's own retry runs. Put a working RetryingDataSource around the resolver: on a googlevideo 403/410, drop the uriCache entry, re-resolve once, then auto-skip. Turn retry-once-then-skip on by default.

(f) Give UriCache a TTL taken from the URL's `expire=` parameter minus 5 minutes. Clear it from a ConnectivityManager default-network callback in PlayerService, because URLs are bound to the IP that fetched them.

(g) Pass yt-dlp's `http_headers` into the DataSpec instead of the Firefox 91 user agent. Precache in ranged 1-10 MiB chunks with maxParallelDownloads = 1.

(h) Take the InnerTube /player pre-call off the hot path. Run it after playback starts, with one current client, to get loudness only.

(i) Pin the exact yt-dlp version for each release. Warm up Python on a background thread at app start.

Phase 2: multi-strategy extractor and Russia support (M-L, about 1 week)

- Resolver chain, trying each in order:
  1. Native InnerTube with the visionOS / ANDROID_VR clients. Mint visitorData per install (from sw.js_data), store it, and remove DEFAULT_VISITOR_DATA and the dead `ytcfg`.
  2. yt-dlp with `extractor_args.youtube.player_client` set to visionos, then tv/mweb, passing the same `visitor_data`.
  3. An optional user-configured Invidious/Piped instance that proxies the audio.
- Before handing a URL to the player, probe its first bytes; if that fails, move to the next strategy.
- Add a bot-check circuit breaker: after one BotCheck, pause extractions for about 2 minutes instead of failing through the whole queue.
- Add one app-wide HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy setting, applied everywhere: the Ktor OkHttp engine, ExoPlayer through OkHttpDataSource sharing the same OkHttpClient, yt-dlp's `proxy` option, and Coil. Extraction and streaming must leave through the same IP.
- Add a "Network check" screen that tests whether youtube.com and googlevideo are reachable and whether a bot check is active, and tells the user plainly when YouTube is blocked and a proxy is needed.
- Replace the broken pip upgrade with a hot update of yt-dlp: publish the wheel as a signed asset on Melogold's GitHub Releases (reusing the self-update code), verify the signature, and load it on the next start.

Phase 3: optional (L)

- Generate PO tokens with a BotGuard WebView, the approach NewPipe uses, and pass them to yt-dlp as `po_token` and to InnerTube.
- Optional YouTube sign-in: capture cookies from a WebView into yt-dlp's `cookiefile`, for age-restricted content. Warn the user that the account could be flagged.
- Live streams: when yt-dlp returns m3u8, use an HlsMediaSource.
- Use the same strategy order and error types in the macOS, Windows and Linux clients. They can run the upstream yt-dlp binary with deno directly.

Much of Phases 1-2 can be adapted from the eXMusic commits listed in the evidence, which are also GPL.

verify:playlist-reorder-bugs.fix_idea:
1) Make positions reliable (S):
- Migration 30->31 that renumbers every playlist densely: `UPDATE SongPlaylistMap SET position=(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM SongPlaylistMap m WHERE m.playlistId=SongPlaylistMap.playlistId AND (m.position<SongPlaylistMap.position OR (m.position=SongPlaylistMap.position AND m.rowid<SongPlaylistMap.rowid)))`.
- Run the same repair in a RoomDatabase.Callback.onOpen, so restored backups and the desktop clients get fixed too.
- Add a non-unique Index(playlistId, position).
- Replace every `position = songCount / index+i` with one SQL append: `INSERT OR IGNORE ... SELECT :songId, :pid, COALESCE(MAX(position)+1,0) FROM SongPlaylistMap WHERE playlistId=:pid`.
- Change move and remove to take songId and read the real position in the same transaction: moveSong(pid, songId, toIndex), and removeSong = DELETE + `UPDATE position=position-1 WHERE position>:p`.
- Apply distinctBy{mediaId} before mapIndexed when importing or syncing.

2) Replace the reorder engine (M):
- Drop compose/reordering in favour of a keyed, optimistic list, e.g. sh.calvin.reorderable. It handles auto-scroll, header items and animateItem.
- Keep a local `snapshotStateList` of song IDs, swap entries while dragging, and write once on drop (moveSong by songId). Ignore database emissions while a drag is in progress.
- Key the state on playlistId, not on the List<Song>.
- Reuse the same component for the queue, and for the desktop client if it is Compose Multiplatform.

3) YouTube-linked playlists (S): set a `locallyModified` flag on any reorder, add or remove. When the flag is set, auto-sync should merge instead of wiping: keep the local order, append new remote songs, and remove songs deleted remotely. Alternatively, make auto-sync off by default.

4) Home tab (S):
- Use `SELECT thumbnailUrl ... AND thumbnailUrl IS NOT NULL` with `List<String?>` and filterNotNull, and add `.catch{}` to the flow.
- Build Piped keys from session.id.
- Move the sort buttons into a single sort dropdown chip, or make "New playlist" a "+" icon, so the header fits at 360dp with long translations.

5) Features (S-M):
- Add an `addedAt` column to SongPlaylistMap. Offer per-playlist view sorts (Manual / Date added / Title / Artist), with drag disabled unless Manual is selected.
- Add a setting for "add new songs to top or bottom".
- A playlist button in the player.

6) Plan ahead for Melogold sync:
- Store a fractional-index sortKey (TEXT, e.g. the rocicorp/Figma fractional-indexing algorithm) plus addedAt, and use tombstones for deletions.
- One drag then updates one row instead of renumbering n rows, and concurrent reorders from Android and desktop merge without scrambling.
- Imports from Apple Music, Spotify or Yandex should add songs with the same append logic.

I checked the code at /Users/maxim/Documents/melogold/melogoldAndroid. The path /Users/maxim/Documents/vitunefork/melogoldAndroid does not exist. Git history shows PlayerService.kt and download.py have not changed since the import commit e493388f. The bug is still there, and nothing in the app, core, providers or compose folders mentions prefetch, preload, LoadControl or PreloadConfiguration.

The blocking path, in app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/service/PlayerService.kt:
- :1357-1469 `createYouTubeDataSourceResolverFactory` runs on ExoPlayer's loader thread whenever neither the disk cache nor UriCache has the track.
- :1403-1405 `runBlocking(Dispatchers.IO) { Innertube.player(...) }` runs first. It is only used for metadata: mimeType, loudnessDb, lastModified and the duration text (:1422-1451).
- providers/innertube/.../requests/Player.kt:17-54 and :64-71 try 4 clients one after another (iOS, Web, AndroidMusic, TV). A client is accepted only if it returns status OK with usable formats, so all 4 round trips happen whenever YouTube refuses them.
- providers/innertube/.../Innertube.kt:53-79 sets no HttpTimeout, so only OkHttp's default per-request timeouts apply.
- Only then does :1408-1412 call `Dependencies.runDownload(mediaId)`. This is a synchronous Chaquopy call with no timeout.
- :1419-1421 blocks again with `runBlocking { findMediaItem }`, which switches to the Main thread (:1066-1068).
- app/.../MainApplication.kt:569-584: Python itself is started lazily (`val py by lazy`, `module by lazy`). So the first song after a cold start also pays for starting CPython and importing yt_dlp. Nothing warms it up in MainApplication.onCreate (:518-540).
- app/src/main/python/download.py:5-10 creates a new `YoutubeDL` on every call. The options set no `extractor_args` (player_client or player_skip), no `cachedir` and no `quiet`. The function returns the whole info dict with `json.dumps(indent=4)` (every format, thumbnail and caption entry), and Kotlin then parses all of it.

Why the next song starts instantly but a jump is slow:
- ExoPlayer is built without a PreloadConfiguration or custom LoadControl (PlayerService.kt:300-313). The next item's resolver therefore runs only when ExoPlayer begins loading the next period near the end of the current track. A jump to any other item pays the full cost in the foreground, which matches #1298.
- The URL cache cannot be used for prefetching. `uriCache` is a default parameter created inside the factory (:1362), and createMediaSourceFactory (:1062-1072) does not pass one, so PlayerService has no reference to it. PrecacheService.kt:174-179 builds a second, separate factory with its own cache.
- UriCache (core/data/.../utils/RingBuffer.kt:24-44) has 16 slots and no TTL. `get` uses `find`, which returns the first match by slot order rather than the newest entry. So a stale googlevideo URL can win over a fresh one. The cache is cleared as a whole only after an unknown error (PlayerService.kt:1466-1468).

This path affects plain YouTube videos (re-uploads, covers, live), which are Melogold's key uncensored source, exactly as much as YouTube Music tracks, because every videoId goes through this same resolver.

The maintainer explains the slowness in the #1089 comments. yt-dlp tries several methods one after another, respects YouTube's wait times, and makes no parallel requests because of rate limits. That makes speculative parallel racing risky. Taking the work off the critical path and prefetching is the safe fix.
verify:slow-song-start.fix_idea:
1) Take InnerTube off the critical path. In the resolver, call only yt-dlp. Fetch the InnerTube metadata (loudness, mimeType, lastModified, duration) afterwards in PlayerService's coroutineScope and update the Format row then. If it has to stay, run it with `async` alongside yt-dlp and cap it with `withTimeoutOrNull(3s)`. Also add ktor's HttpTimeout to Innertube.baseClient.

2) Make each yt-dlp call cheaper:
- Warm up Python early: run `Dependencies.py` and import the module on Dispatchers.IO from PlayerService.onCreate or MainApplication.onCreate.
- In download.py, keep one module-level YoutubeDL so the player JS and challenge solutions stay cached in memory. Set `cachedir` to the app's filesDir so they also survive restarts. Add `quiet` and `noplaylist`, and a configurable `extractor_args.youtube.player_client` (a short, benchmarked list, overridable remotely through Melogold's server config) plus `player_skip` where it is safe.
- Return only id, url, format_id, filesize/filesize_approx, abr, duration and the http_headers, not the whole info dict.
- In Kotlin, wrap the call in a timeout (a Future with get(20, SECONDS)) and raise a real error instead of VideoIdMismatch.

3) Prefetch (the main user-visible gain):
- Hoist the UriCache into a PlayerService field and pass it to the factory.
- Give each entry a TTL taken from googlevideo's `expire` query parameter minus a margin, and allow evicting a single key.
- In onMediaItemTransition and onTimelineChanged, resolve the next 2-3 non-local, non-cached queue items in the background: one at a time, with a small delay, deduplicated through a Mutex-guarded map of in-flight Deferreds. The resolver then awaits an in-flight job instead of starting a second yt-dlp call.
- Also resolve on user intent that predicts a jump: long-press or opening a queue item, and the first item of a list the user just opened.
- Additionally call `player.setPreloadConfiguration(ExoPlayer.PreloadConfiguration(10_000_000))` (media3 1.11 supports it) so the first chunk of the next item is buffered in advance.

4) Resilience: on a 403 from a cached URL, evict only that key and re-resolve once, instead of clearing everything through handleUnknownErrors. Show a "Resolving stream…" state in the player so the wait is visible.

Desktop clients should reuse the same design: one warm resolver process, a TTL URL cache and next-N prefetch.

The bug is still present. The task's path /Users/maxim/Documents/vitunefork/melogoldAndroid does not exist, so I checked /Users/maxim/Documents/melogold/melogoldAndroid. - app/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/android/utils/ExoPlayer.kt:50-66 (CatchingDataSourceFactory, applied at PlayerService.kt:1466-1468 via .handleUnknownErrors{uriCache.clear()}) wraps any open() exception that is not a PlaybackException into PlaybackException("Unknown playback error"). That includes HTTP 403 and 416, timeouts and UnknownHost.
- PlaybackException is not an IOException. Media3 1.11.1 Loader$LoadTask wraps it in Loader$UnexpectedLoaderException, and DefaultLoadErrorHandlingPolicy.getRetryDelayMsFor returns TIME_UNSET for that type, meaning no retry. I verified both with javap on the cached media3 jars.
- The only policy override is isEligibleForFallback (PlayerService.kt:1075-1077).
- Thumbnail.kt:250-263 maps error.cause.cause of type PlaybackException to R.string.error_unknown_playback. That is exactly the "An unknown playback error has occurred" text in #1073, #869, #1301, #606 and #1424. Network errors also show this text, because the UnknownHost cause is hidden one level deeper.
- onPlayerError (PlayerService.kt:526-555) auto-recovers only HTTP 416. Otherwise it calls seekToNextMediaItem when skipOnError is on (:538-541), which is the "random skip" in #587, or it just stops.
- Recovery happens only on a media-item transition (maybeRecoverPlaybackError :504, :573-575) or when the user dismisses the error (Thumbnail.kt:266). That is why "pause/play fixes it" in #1310 and #606: prepare() re-resolves after uriCache.clear().

ROOT CAUSE 2: why it stops at fixed points (30 s / 524 KB, 59 s / 1 MB).
- The player reads in 512 KiB chunks (DEFAULT_CHUNK_LENGTH, PlayerService.kt:1336; ranged() :1373-1382). Each chunk boundary is a new open() through the resolver, which reuses the URL from UriCache (:1398-1401).
- UriCache (core/data/src/main/kotlin/app/vitune/core/data/utils/RingBuffer.kt:24-44) has 16 slots, no TTL and no per-key remove. Upstream deleted validUntil/expiresInSeconds when it switched to yt-dlp (commit 1b83f289). The same commit deleted the retryIf(403), handleRangeErrors and withFallback wrappers, which is why ExoPlayer.kt:22-48 and :82-181 are now dead code (no callers).
- So any 403 at a boundary kills playback at 524288 B, 1 MiB, and so on.
- Live probe, 2026-09-23. I resolved a URL with our bundled yt-dlp 2026.08.19: client c=VISIONOS, itag 251. The URL is signed with ip and expire in sparams, and expire - now = 6.0 h. A tampered expire gives 403.
- Consequences: a URL older than 6 h (long pause, or replaying something still in the 16 slots) fails with 403, and so does switching between Wi-Fi and mobile data mid-song (the "only on 4G" comment in #606). A 1 h live set or concert re-upload has about 110 boundaries, so it is especially exposed. This matters for our plain-YouTube use case.
- The August 2026 wave (#1433, #1417, #1424) came from yt-dlp 2026.07.04 using android_vr, whose URLs 403 on any range past about 1,048,000 bytes (philippe44/LMS-YouTube#90, anxdpanic/plugin.video.youtube#1481). Our build pins yt-dlp>=2026.08.19 (app/build.gradle.kts:175), whose defaults are ('visionos','web') (bundled _video.py:143). In my probe, chunks past 1 MiB returned 206, so that specific cap is currently avoided. The next YouTube change will hit the same no-retry path.

ROOT CAUSE 3: precache is slow and looks stuck (#1417, #1424).
- PrecacheService.kt:174-179 passes chunkLength = null, so ranged() returns the DataSpec unchanged. At position 0 with unknown length, DefaultHttpDataSource sends no Range header.
- Probe result: a request with no Range header got 200 but was throttled to about 32 KB/s (1.9 MB in 60 s, curl timed out). Bounded or open-ended Range requests got 206 at about 2.4 MB/s (the whole 3.4 MB in 1.3 s). So precache crawls, which looks like "stuck at ~1 MB", and on flaky networks it dies.
- minRetryCount = 1 (:183).

ROOT CAUSE 4: "Pause cache" breaks new songs (#606).
- CacheState.kt:165-169 falls back to upstream only if the exception `is ReadOnlyException`. But ConditionalReadOnlyCache.startFile (Cache.kt:20-23) is called inside CacheDataSink.open, which wraps the exception in CacheDataSink$CacheDataSinkException (verified in bytecode). So the check never matches, and the first open of an uncached song fails with "unknown playback error".
- ConditionalReadOnlyCache.releaseHoleSpan (Cache.kt:30-33) throws, so the hole-span lock leaks. Later opens then bypass the cache, which is why the song plays after pause/play.

- ranged() (:1373-1382) uses uriPositionOffset (0) instead of position. It therefore asks for up to 512 KiB past the current position even near the end, so the last chunk overshoots EOF; the probe got 206 with fewer bytes, and 416 exactly at EOF. The hand-built "Range: bytes=start-(start+length)" header is off by one. That is masked, because DefaultHttpDataSource overwrites Range from position and length (verified: setRequestProperty for custom headers first, then buildRangeRequestHeader). The 416 hack is at :529-536.

verify:midtrack-stream-failures.fix_idea:
Rework the stream layer once in :core/data or a shared module and reuse the same rules in the desktop clients. The googlevideo rules are the same everywhere: 6 h expiry, IP-bound URLs, unranged requests throttled, 416 at EOF.

1. Let I/O errors be retried (S). Delete CatchingDataSourceFactory and the dead ExoPlayer.kt:22-181 factories. Replace them with a thin wrapper that, on InvalidResponseCodeException 403/410, SocketTimeout or UnknownHost:
   - removes only that mediaId's URL,
   - rethrows the original IOException, so the Loader retries and the next open re-resolves.
   Add a custom LoadErrorHandlingPolicy:
   - 403/410: retry at 0 ms, up to 3 times.
   - Network errors: exponential backoff 1-8 s.
   - getMinimumLoadableRetryCount = 6.
   Throw resolver failures (Unplayable and similar) as IOException subclasses so ParserException and FileNotFound-style errors are still not retried.

2. Replace UriCache with StreamUrlCache (S):
   - Map<mediaId, Entry(candidates, itag, contentLength, expiresAt)>, synchronized, with remove(key).
   - expiresAt = min(expire query param, now + 5 h) - 60 s.
   - Also drop the entry when the network changes: a ConnectivityManager callback clears the whole cache, because URLs are IP-bound.

3. Recover mid-track automatically in onPlayerError (S), before skipOnError:
   - Per-mediaId attempt counter: 2-3 attempts, cleared on transition.
   - On each attempt: streamUrlCache.remove(id), player.prepare(), play(). The position is preserved.
   - Show the error or skip only after that.
   - Map the UI message by walking the whole cause chain with findCause, not cause.cause.

4. Fix ranged() (S):
   - start = dataSpec.position.
   - length = min(contentLength - position, chunk).
   - If position >= contentLength, return an end-of-stream spec.
   - Drop the manual Range header.
   - The isCached check should use the same clamped length.
   - Then remove the 416 hack.

5. Precache (S): never send an unbounded request. Add a ChunkedHttpDataSource that internally loops bounded requests of 1-4 MiB inside one logical open()/read(). Use it for both player and DownloadManager, which also removes the fragile "EOF every 512 KiB, Loader retries" trick. Set minRetryCount to 5. Surface a per-song failed state in the UI.

6. Pause cache (S):
   - Build two CacheDataSource.Factory instances: read-write, and read-only (setCacheWriteDataSinkFactory(null)).
   - Pick one per open() from PlayerPreferences.pauseCache.
   - Delete ConditionalReadOnlyCache and ReadOnlyException.

7. Cache integrity (S-M):
   - Pin the itag once a song has cached spans: yt-dlp format "<itag>/bestaudio". Store the chosen itag and contentLength in Format and only update them when the cache is empty.
   - If the itag or clen changes, call cache.removeResource(id) before streaming.
   - Optionally key the cache as "$id:$itag".

8. Resolver robustness (M):
   - Wrap the Innertube and yt-dlp calls in withTimeout, about 20 s, and rethrow as IOException.
   - Resolve 2-3 candidates (yt-dlp bestaudio plus an alternative format or client via extractor_args, and Innertube direct URLs). Rotate candidates only while no spans of that id are cached.
   - Pass the yt-dlp format http_headers to the HTTP data source.
   - Accept filesize_approx; otherwise probe with Range: bytes=0-0 and read Content-Range.
   - Auto-upgrade yt-dlp in the background on repeated 403s (currently only a manual button, OtherSettings.kt:284). This is how the August 2026 android_vr break would have healed without an app release.

9. Add a debug log line per failure (http code, itag, c= client, URL age, byte offset), so we can diagnose the next YouTube change quickly.

   - a storage bar that shows download size separately from the stream cache in CacheSettings

A small collector enqueues missing songs when Favorites changes (optional "Auto-download liked songs" setting) or when songs are added to a collection flagged autoDownload, including after YouTube playlist sync. STORE POLICIES THAT AFFECT MELOGOLD
- Homebrew (docs.brew.sh/Package-Acceptance-Policy): a cask the owner submits to the official repo needs at least 90 forks, 90 watchers or 225 stars, and a repo younger than 30 days is normally refused. Our repos do not qualify, so we would start with our own tap.
- Homebrew (Acceptable-Casks): the app must pass Gatekeeper, which means Developer ID signing and notarization.
- Homebrew (Cask-Cookbook): `auto_updates true` is the documented way to mark apps that update themselves, such as Sparkle apps.
- Flathub: runs an external data checker every 2 hours that opens update PRs automatically, so a Flathub app can stay current without its own updater.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE FOR MELOGOLD
Plain YouTube playback depends on the stream extractor (yt-dlp on Android), which breaks every few weeks. If a package manager lags behind our releases, playback breaks for those users. So extractor freshness has to be designed alongside the updater decision, not left to it.

1. Shared design (all clients)
- At build time, compile in a distribution channel: MELOGOLD_CHANNEL = github-appimage | github-deb | github-rpm | flathub | aur | nix | homebrew | velopack | scoop | winget | fdroid.
- If the channel is missing, treat the build as a package-manager build.
- Add a runtime check as a fallback, in case someone repackages a GitHub build.
- Updater behaviour by channel:
  - Our own artifacts: download and install the update.
  - Package-manager builds: show "Update with: <exact command>" (`flatpak update`, `brew upgrade --cask melogold`, `winget upgrade Melogold.Melogold`, `scoop update melogold`), or stay silent.
- Pick the IDs once and never change them (Pear's rename broke brew, winget and Scoop):
  - app ID io.github.melogold_app.Melogold (or app.melogold.Melogold if we own that domain);
  - winget ID Melogold.Melogold;
  - cask and Scoop name melogold.
- Server: publish a minimum/recommended client version per platform, and keep the sync API compatible with a few older versions, because package managers deliver updates days late.
- Extractor: keep yt-dlp updates separate from app releases.
  - Flatpak: ship yt-dlp as its own module with x-checker-data (pypi), so Flathub's bot opens a PR within about 2 hours.
  - AUR/Nix: depend on the distro's yt-dlp package.
  - Our own builds: an optional, hash-pinned yt-dlp download into the data directory that packagers can switch off.

2. Linux (Rust)
- Put the updater behind a cargo feature `self-update` that is off by default. CI turns it on only for the AppImage.
- The AppImage updates through zsync: embed update info "gh-releases-zsync|melogold-app|melogoldLinux|latest|Melogold-*-x86_64.AppImage.zsync", and publish the .zsync file with each release.
- Runtime check:
  - FLATPAK_ID set, or /.flatpak-info exists: Flatpak.
  - SNAP set: Snap.
  - APPIMAGE set: the AppImage, so self-update is allowed.
  - Executable under /usr, /opt or /nix/store and not writable: system package, so only notify.
- Add packaging/flatpak/io.github.melogold_app.Melogold.yml:
  - GNOME runtime, Rust sources vendored with flatpak-cargo-generator;
  - permissions: network, wayland, fallback-x11, pulseaudio, dri, and own-name org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.Melogold.
- Also add a metainfo.xml and a .desktop file. The desktop file's basename, the GApplication application_id (which becomes the Wayland app_id), the MPRIS DesktopEntry and the icon name must all equal the app ID (see Pear #2806). Rename the existing hicolor icons to the app ID.
- Submit to Flathub. The name "Melogold" and our own icon satisfy the trademark rule; do not put "YouTube" in the name or icon.
- Publish AUR melogold-bin (repackaging the deb or AppImage) and melogold (built from source, feature off). Later, add a nixpkgs package.

3. Windows (.NET/WinUI 3)
- Use Velopack: a per-user install under %LocalAppData%, delta updates from GitHub Releases, and a portable zip.
- The updater stays off when:
  - the app runs as MSIX (a package identity exists);
  - the executable path contains \scoop\apps\ (Scoop manages the version folder);
  - the path is under \chocolatey\lib\.
- For Velopack installs, make sure each update rewrites DisplayVersion in the HKCU Uninstall key, so `winget upgrade` sees the right version.
- CI: on each release, run winget-releaser/wingetcreate (PR to winget-pkgs with the fixed ID), and push a Scoop manifest to melogold-app/scoop-bucket with checkver github and autoupdate.

4. macOS (Swift, no iOS)
- Sparkle, with an EdDSA key; generate_appcast in CI and serve appcast.xml from releases/latest/download.
- Signing: Developer ID plus notarytool, which Homebrew's Gatekeeper rule requires. Budget for the Apple Developer Program and note that payment from Russia may be a blocker.
- Tap melogold-app/homebrew-tap with Casks/melogold.rb containing `auto_updates true`, so `brew upgrade` leaves the app to Sparkle unless the user passes --greedy. CI bumps the cask on each release. Submit to the official cask repo once past 225 stars, 90 forks or 90 watchers and 30 days of age.

5. Android (the same rule; this one can be done now)
- Point About.kt:63-64 at melogold-app/melogoldAndroid and restart version numbering.
- Pick the APK that matches Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS[0], or ship a universal APK.
- Allow in-app update only when the signing certificate's SHA-256 equals our GitHub release key (the NewPipe approach). F-Droid and IzzyOnDroid rebuilds use other keys and would fail with a signature mismatch anyway.
- If getInstallSourceInfo().installingPackageName is F-Droid (org.fdroid.*), Droid-ify, Neo Store, Obtainium (dev.imranr.obtainium) or Aurora, show "Updates are managed by X".
- Use product flavors: github (updater + REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES) and fdroid (no updater), because F-Droid does not accept self-updaters.
- Replace the fastlane metadata that still says ViTune.

Effort: the updater with channel checks is M per client, the Flatpak/Flathub submission is M (plus weeks of review), and AppImage zsync, AUR, winget, the Scoop bucket and the Homebrew tap are each S. Across all platforms that is L.

1. Local stream server (the core piece, needed for every protocol). Add a small HTTP server (ktor-server-cio or NanoHTTPD) owned by PlayerService, bound to the Wi-Fi interface IP, with a random token in the path:
- `/s/{token}/{videoId}.m4a` reuses the existing resolver (PlayerService.kt:1356-1468). It serves from SimpleCache when the track is cached, otherwise streams googlevideo in ranged chunks and passes the receiver's Range header through. For cast targets, request `bestaudio[ext=m4a]/bestaudio` (AAC is what Sonos and most DLNA renderers accept).
- `/l/{token}/{id}` serves local `content://` tracks.
- `/art/{token}/{id}.jpg` serves artwork.

This avoids the VPN IP-lock and throttling problems, expired URLs, https-only and long-URL failures on DLNA renderers, and makes cached and local tracks castable. Offer "direct URL" only as an optional battery saver for Chromecast/FCast, with automatic fallback to the server on a receiver load error. Hold a WifiLock and keep the existing mediaPlayback foreground service while casting.

2. Protocols without Google Play Services, from one MIT library. Use FUTO's FCast sender SDK (Kotlin: `org.futo.gitlab.videostreaming.fcast-sdk-jitpack:sender-sdk-minimal`, as used by Grayjay).
- Its NsdDeviceDiscoverer finds both `_fcast._tcp` and `_googlecast._tcp` devices.
- It drives the Chromecast Default Media Receiver itself, so it works on de-Googled phones and needs no gms/foss flavor split (unlike Metrolist's GMS CastPlayer).

For DLNA/UPnP and Sonos, write a small SSDP discovery plus AVTransport/RenderingControl SOAP client (roughly 500 lines, or use jUPnP):
- SetAVTransportURI with DIDL-Lite metadata and `http-get:*:audio/mp4:*`;
- SetNextAVTransportURI for gapless playback;
- GetPositionInfo polling.

Add the ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, ACCESS_WIFI_STATE and CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE permissions, a MulticastLock, and the Android 17 local-network permission if it applies.

3. Player integration.
- Write `RemoteDevicePlayer : SimpleBasePlayer` (Media3) per protocol, and a switching Player that the service and Binder expose. Change `Binder.player` at PlayerService.kt:1124 to `Player` and guard the 2 `audioSessionId` call sites.
- The phone stays in charge of the queue: on connect, snapshot queue, index and position, pause the local ExoPlayer and load the current item at that position. On ENDED (or a pre-queued next item), load the next one.
- Call `mediaSession.setPlaybackToRemote(VolumeProvider)` so hardware volume keys control the receiver.
- Re-wire what depends on the local player:
  - emit history Events from the remote player (PlayerService.kt:461 only fires for ExoPlayer);
  - send SponsorBlock seeks and the sleep timer to the device;
  - hide normalization, bass boost, reverb, skip-silence and the equalizer while casting.
- Explicitly test long playlists; this is where Metrolist breaks (#3892, #4359).

4. UI.
- A cast button next to the ellipsis in the player (ui/screens/player/Player.kt:563-585) and in the mini player.
- A device sheet grouped by protocol.
- An "also keep playing here" toggle (Pear #113).

5. Melogold Connect (differentiator). List the user's other signed-in Melogold devices (desktop, Android TV via the existing LEANBACK entry) as targets. Send {videoId, queue, position, play/pause} over the LAN or relayed by the sync server; this is metadata only, which fits the server model. The target resolves its own stream, so no proxying is needed.

6. Video, phase 2 (the "plain YouTube is first-class" goal). Cast actual video to TVs: progressive mp4 (itag 18), the HLS manifest for live streams, or a DASH manifest served by the local server. FCast and Chromecast both accept HLS/DASH.

- Windows (C#/WinUI 3): the FCastSenderSDKDotnet NuGet package (as in Grayjay Desktop) plus an SSDP/AVTransport client or Windows.Media.Casting CastingDevicePicker for DLNA, with a Kestrel stream server.

- ViMusic #40: closed. The maintainer's reply was "playback is already gapless".
- Metrolist #345: completed 2026-02 using a secondaryPlayer swap plus a volume ramp (MusicService.kt scheduleCrossfade/startCrossfade/performCrossfadeSwap, about lines 4766-4990). It skips crossfade when the next track is on the same album.

verify:crossfade-gapless.fix_idea:
1) Fade on pause, resume and stop (S). Add one volume owner in PlayerService: player.volume = userGain * fadeFactor, with a fadeTo(target, ms) coroutine (about 20 steps, equal-power curve) that is cancelled when a new fade starts. Replace `player.volume = 1f` at :658 with a call through it. Add Binder.pause(fade = true) and play(fade = true): fade out, then pause, then restore the volume; for play, set volume 0, play, fade in. Route every pause and play call listed in the evidence through it, and give the sleep timer (:1166) a longer 5-10 s fade. Leave audio-focus loss and BECOMING_NOISY instant; ExoPlayer handles those internally, as it should. New setting pauseFadeMs (0-1000, default 300) in PlayerSettings.kt's Audio group.

2) Gapless hardening (S-M).
(a) Pull the resolver body (:1398-1456) into a StreamResolver.resolve(id) with withTimeout, plus a TTL on UriCache taken from the googlevideo `expire` value. On onMediaItemTransition and onTimelineChanged, resolve the next 1-2 queue items in the background. Optionally write their first 512 KiB into SimpleCache with CacheWriter, so manual skips and crossfades start instantly.
(b) Call player.setPreloadConfiguration(ExoPlayer.PreloadConfiguration(10_000_000)) (available in media3 1.11.1) so the next item prepares earlier.
(c) Call setOutputSampleRateHz(48000) on the SonicAudioProcessor at :1112. Every source then produces the same PCM format, and DefaultAudioSink can reuse its AudioTrack across items with no reinit gap.
(d) Look up the next track's loudness ahead of time and set the LoudnessEnhancer gain at the transition, not in async flows. Add a "gapless albums" option: when current and next share an album, turn off crossfade and keep the gain step small. Metrolist's isNextItemGapless check (albumTitle equality) is a working example.

3) Crossfade (M). Keep binder.player stable and use a throwaway tail player for the outgoing track instead of swapping players:
- Schedule a PlayerMessage at duration minus X. Reschedule it on seek, transition, timeline change and speed change.
- At the trigger, build tailPlayer = ExoPlayer.Builder(this, createRendersFactory(), createMediaSourceFactory()) with handleAudioFocus = false and setAudioSessionId(player.audioSessionId), so LoudnessEnhancer, BassBoost, Reverb and EQ also apply to it. Give it the current item and position and copy the playback parameters. It reads from cache through the fast path at :1384-1396.
- Ramp the tail player's volume 1 to 0 while the main player calls seekToNextMediaItem() (ExoPlayer reuses the preloaded period) and ramps 0 to 1. Release the tail player at the end.
- Pause or resume both players together. Cancel the crossfade on manual seek.
- Skip it for repeat-one, tracks shorter than 2X, the last item, same-album gapless, or when the next item is not resolved yet.
- Settings: crossfadeSeconds (0 = off, 1-12) and crossfadeOnManualSkip (a short 1-2 s crossfade).
This keeps MediaSession, notification, UI listeners, history and radio all bound to one player.

4) Automix, DJ-style beat matching (XL). Defer it; a crossfade plus trimming leading and trailing silence covers most of what users ask for.

For desktop: if the clients use libmpv, gapless-audio=weak gives gapless for free; crossfade needs the same two-decoder approach there.
